components.name: Band
components.summary: The layout primitives: **Main**, **PageContainer**, **Stack**, **Grid**, **Section**, for a search page **StickyTop** and **SplitView**, and **Sticky** and **Dock**. Screens use them for every width, gap and column, so a screen never writes layout CSS and stays on the 4px grid and AcmeCo's own layout values (decision 34). Gaps are named steps (`2xs` 4px … `3xl` 64px, plus AcmeCo's fluid `block` and `section` gaps), never numbers.

props.name: children
props.description: What the band holds: usually a PageContainer, so its content keeps the page's width.

props.name: tone
props.description: default: white. subtle: AcmeCo's light grey (a results bar).

props.name: divider
props.description: A thin line under the band (the gallery's title band and filter bar).

whenToUse: **Main** once per page, between GlobalHeader and Footer, with a PageContainer inside it. `paddingBlock` (default `xl`, 32px) sets the space under the header and above the footer.
**PageContainer** once per band of the page (header, main, footer), around the content that should line up with the page edges.
**Stack** for anything in a line: fields in a form (`md`), cards in a list (`lg`), a row of buttons (`horizontal`, `xs`), sections of a page (`section`).
**Grid** for columns that collapse: result cards (`columns={{ base: 1, md: 2, xl: 3 }}`), the property detail page's content and contact sidebar (`template="main-aside"`).
**Section** for each titled part of a page; pass the heading's id as `labelledBy`.
**StickyTop** around GlobalHeader and a search page's filter bar, so they stay at the top as on AcmeCo's results. Give the bar a PageContainer with `paddingBlock="xs"`.
**Sticky** as the aside of Grid's `main-aside` (it must be the grid's direct child), around the contact box.
**Band** for a strip across the window: a white title band or filter bar (`divider` adds the line under it), or AcmeCo's grey results bar (`tone="subtle"`). Put a PageContainer inside it.
**PageContainer** `width="gallery"` for the gallery results (cards two by two, about 1,032px wide).

**SplitView** `placement="top"` puts the map in a 360px band above a full-width list that stays in view while the cards scroll beneath it (a proposal, decision 45); give the list a Grid so the cards sit in rows.

**Dock** once per page, after the Footer, around the Assistant (with `clearBar` when the page has a bar); `placement="bar"` for a phone's bar of actions fixed to the bottom (a listing's Call and Message), which keeps the page's end clear of it.
**StickyTop** `fixedOnPhones` keeps a listing's header and title bar at the top on phones too.
**Hide** `as="span"` hides part of a line, such as a heading's address on phones.

**Stack** options: `fill="first"` gives the first child the space left (a search box beside a button); `scrollBelow="md"` keeps a phone's pills on one line, scrolling sideways; `gap={{ base: 'none', md: 'lg' }}` changes the gap from 768px.
**Hide** when a phone needs a different arrangement of the same controls (`below="md"` / `above="md"`); hidden content is gone for screen readers too, so each width must still have every control.
**StickyTop** is fixed from 768px only; on phones it scrolls away so the list has the screen. **SplitView** `compactAside="hidden"` hides the map on phones until a Map link shows it.
**SplitView** straight inside Main (full width, not in a PageContainer) with `aside={<MapPlaceholder …/>}` and the results as its children. Below 1024px the aside is a 240px band above the list.
whenNotToUse: Not inside components: they bring their own layout and tokens. The primitives are for screens.
Don't nest Stacks to fake columns; use Grid.
Don't use StickyTop on ordinary pages: a fixed band takes room from the content, a third of a phone's screen when a filter bar wraps.
Don't add a margin or a `style` to space things out; pick a gap. If no step fits, that's a gap in the system: log it (see the screen-building guide).

props.description: The visible label. Also the button's accessible name.

props.name: variant

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the width of its container.

props.description: Red border; pair it with an error message (CheckboxGroup shows one).

props.name: value
props.description: Required inside a CheckboxGroup: what this option means in the group's value.

whenToUse: Any number of options from a short list: a CheckboxGroup with a label ("Space use").
A single yes/no choice that takes effect when a form is sent: one Checkbox.
"Select all" over a partly checked list: `isIndeterminate` shows a dash.
whenNotToUse: Exactly one choice from a few: a TabSelector, or a radio group (later).
Exactly one choice from many: Select.
A setting that takes effect immediately: a switch (not in v1).

components.name: CheckboxGroup
components.summary: Checkboxes let people pick any number of options (space use, amenities), or confirm one thing ("Email me new listings like this"). It's already AcmeCo's most consistent control, so its look is kept; the border is darkened to pass contrast, and checked becomes the dark blue fill with a white check. **CheckboxGroup** gives a set of checkboxes one label, hint and error.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible label, read before each option ("Space use, Office, checkbox").

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, the group is invalid: each box gets a red border, and this message (with an icon) is linked to the group.

whenToUse: Any number of options from a short list: a CheckboxGroup with a label ("Space use").
A single yes/no choice that takes effect when a form is sent: one Checkbox.
"Select all" over a partly checked list: `isIndeterminate` shows a dash.
whenNotToUse: Exactly one choice from a few: a TabSelector, or a radio group (later).
Exactly one choice from many: Select.
A setting that takes effect immediately: a switch (not in v1).

components.name: ChipGroup
components.summary: Chips show values someone has chosen, such as states in a location filter or active filters above results, and let them remove each one. They keep AcmeCo's look (the light-blue tag with a small ×, as in the expanded filters panel), measured from the live site's CSS.

props.name: label
props.description: Always required: what the chips are ("Selected states"); the list's accessible name.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label above the chips. Usually hidden: the field or heading around them explains them.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Called with the ids removed (by the x button, or Delete / Backspace on a focused chip). Omit to make chips not removable.

whenToUse: Selected values in a multi-select field ("Colorado ×", "Texas ×").
Active filters above results, so people can see and undo them.
whenNotToUse: Labels that can't be removed: use a Badge.
Choosing options: Checkbox, Select or TabSelector. Chips show what's already chosen.
Actions: use a Button.

components.name: ChoiceCards
components.summary: One choice from a handful of options, drawn as cards: AcmeCo's language-and-region and currency choices ("English / United Kingdom", "Euro / EUR €"). A radio group underneath, so the choice is announced, not just shown in blue. The selected card keeps AcmeCo's light blue fill and 2px blue border (decision 36).

props.name: label
props.description: What's being chosen ("Language and region"): the group's accessible name.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label above the cards. Hidden by default when a heading or tab already says it.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns on wider screens (default 3); at 450px and below, at most 2.

whenToUse: Four to about twelve options where a second line helps tell them apart (a language and its region).
Where all the options should be visible at once, in a grid.
whenNotToUse: Two to four short options in one line: a TabSelector.
Long lists: a Select.
Several choices at once: a CheckboxGroup.
Actions or links: each card sets a value, it doesn't navigate.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal dialog: it blocks the page until it's closed. Header with a required title and a Close button, a body that scrolls, and an optional footer for actions. Two sizes; full screen on phones. Used by sign-in, the contact form and the filters panel.

props.name: title
props.description: Required: shown as the heading and names the dialog for screen readers.

props.name: children
props.description: The body. A function receives `close`, for content that finishes the task itself (choosing a language).

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions, in a footer that stays put while the body scrolls. A function receives `close`.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` 500px (single-column forms), `lg` 768px (two columns, filters). Full screen at 768px and below.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Clicking the backdrop closes the dialog (default). Turn it off for dialogs holding a form, so a stray click doesn't lose what someone typed. Escape and Close always work (decision 28).

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Leave both unset when the dialog sits inside a DialogTrigger.

whenToUse: A short task that must be finished or dismissed before going back to the page: contact a broker, sign in, set filters.
Put it in a `DialogTrigger` with the button that opens it; or control it with `isOpen` and `onOpenChange`.
`md` (500px) for single-column forms; `lg` (768px) for two columns or many controls (sign-in, filters).
whenNotToUse: Anything that doesn't need to block the page: use inline content, a popover (Select) or a new page.
Long reading or multi-step flows: give them a page.
Not for confirmations or alerts yet (`alertdialog`): none were observed on AcmeCo; add one when a flow needs it.

components.name: Disclosure
components.summary: A button that shows or hides a group: the Search group in AcmeCo's menu (For Lease, For Sale, Auctions, Businesses, Find a Broker), and later accordions. A 40px row in semibold with a chevron that turns when open (decision 36).

props.name: title
props.description: The button's text: what the group holds ("Search").

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Wrap the button in a heading of this level, when the group is a section of the page (an accordion). Leave unset in menus.

whenToUse: A group of links or content that most people don't need every time (a menu's sub-links, an FAQ answer, extra details).
With `headingLevel` when each group is a section of the page (an accordion), so it appears in the page outline.
whenNotToUse: Navigating to another page: a link.
Switching between panels of the same kind: Tabs.
Hiding something everyone needs (prices, contact details).

components.name: FactList
components.summary: Label / value rows: AcmeCo's property facts ("Building Size 22,400 SF"). The audit found seven designs for this one row on property pages (F21); this is one. It closes the property page's Property Facts gap and fills the space cards on phones (decision 47).

props.name: items
props.description: The facts, in reading order.

props.name: columns
props.description: 2: two facts on a row where there's room (560px or wider), one below that.

whenToUse: For facts about one thing, each a short label and a short value: a property's size, type and year, a space's size, rate and use.
`columns={2}` for a longer list in a wide column: two facts on a row from 560px, one below that, as on AcmeCo's phone.
whenNotToUse: Not to compare several things fact by fact (all the spaces in a building): that's a table.
Not for long text; a value is a word, a number or a short phrase.
Not for form fields: those are TextField, Select and the rest.

components.name: FilterButton
components.summary: AcmeCo's search-bar pills. **FilterButton** is the pill: a filter's name (or its value once set), an optional icon and count (All Filters: sliders and a blue "2"), and a chevron when it opens a panel. **FilterMenu** is a FilterButton that opens a panel of choices (a Popover) and, once set, shows its value and clears in place ("Office, Coworking ✕"). Same height, shape and type as the compact Select beside them, so the whole bar is one family (decision 40). Found missing by the search results screen (gaps 1–3).

props.name: children
props.description: The filter's name ("Rent"), or what it's set to ("$20–$40 /SF/YR"). Also its accessible name.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon before the label (All Filters' sliders), from the registry. Hidden from screen readers.

props.name: count
props.description: How many filters are set (All Filters): a blue count, read as "2 applied".

props.name: hasMenu
props.description: Shows a chevron: pressing opens a panel (the default). False for a pill that acts directly.

props.name: isActive
props.description: The filter is set: dark border on light grey, as AcmeCo's.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Shows only the icon in a round button (the phone's filter button); the label stays its accessible name.

whenToUse: **FilterMenu** for each filter in a search bar: a list of choices (CheckboxGroup), a range (two TextFields), a single choice.

Pass `value` once it's set: one choice by name ("Office"), **"Multiple"** for two or more (the chips under the bar list them), a range with its unit ("$20–$40 /SF/YR"), and `onClear` so the pill clears in place.
**FilterButton** with `count` and `hasMenu={false}` for All Filters, opening a Dialog with every filter; on phones use `iconOnly` (a round button with the count over its corner, as AcmeCo's).
Below 768px every pill is AcmeCo's phone size (40px, 16px text, no chevron); put them in a Stack with `scrollBelow="md"` so they stay on one line and scroll sideways.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing one value from a short list where a Select fits ("For Lease"): use the compact Select.
Not as a page's main action: use Button.
Don't put more than a few words in a set pill; the chips under the bar can list everything.

components.name: FilterMenu
components.summary: AcmeCo's search-bar pills. **FilterButton** is the pill: a filter's name (or its value once set), an optional icon and count (All Filters: sliders and a blue "2"), and a chevron when it opens a panel. **FilterMenu** is a FilterButton that opens a panel of choices (a Popover) and, once set, shows its value and clears in place ("Office, Coworking ✕"). Same height, shape and type as the compact Select beside them, so the whole bar is one family (decision 40). Found missing by the search results screen (gaps 1–3).

props.name: label
props.description: The filter's name ("Space Use"): the pill's text until it's set, and the panel's name.

props.name: value
props.description: What it's set to, in a few words ("Office, Coworking"): shown instead of the label, with a clear button.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Clears the filter (the x in the pill). Without it a set pill shows its chevron instead.

props.name: children
props.description: The panel: checkboxes, a range, and so on. A function receives `close`.

whenToUse: **FilterMenu** for each filter in a search bar: a list of choices (CheckboxGroup), a range (two TextFields), a single choice.

Pass `value` once it's set: one choice by name ("Office"), **"Multiple"** for two or more (the chips under the bar list them), a range with its unit ("$20–$40 /SF/YR"), and `onClear` so the pill clears in place.
**FilterButton** with `count` and `hasMenu={false}` for All Filters, opening a Dialog with every filter; on phones use `iconOnly` (a round button with the count over its corner, as AcmeCo's).
Below 768px every pill is AcmeCo's phone size (40px, 16px text, no chevron); put them in a Stack with `scrollBelow="md"` so they stay on one line and scroll sideways.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing one value from a short list where a Select fits ("For Lease"): use the compact Select.
Not as a page's main action: use Button.
Don't put more than a few words in a set pill; the chips under the bar can list everything.

components.name: Heading
components.summary: The headings of a page and its sections in the system's type styles: **display** (hero), **heading-1**, **heading-2** and **heading-3**. The `level` (h1–h6) sets the page's outline, which screen readers navigate by; the `size` sets the look, so the two can differ (a section's h2 can look like heading-3). No margins: the layout primitives set the space around it. Found missing by the page shell pilot (gap 1, decision 38).

props.name: level
props.description: Its place in the page's outline: 1 for the page's one h1, then 2, 3… in order, never skipping.

props.name: size
props.description: How it looks, independent of the level (an h2 can look like heading-3). Defaults: level 1 → heading-1, 2 → heading-2, 3 and below → heading-3. display is for a hero. One size, or one per width ({ base: 'heading-3', md: 'heading-1' }: smaller on phones).

props.name: align
props.description: start (the default) or center: a title bar's lines centred, also when they wrap.

props.name: id
props.description: For Section's labelledBy, so the section is named by its heading.

whenToUse: **Level 1, once per page:** the page's title (heading-1; display for a hero).
**Levels 2 and 3** for sections and the parts inside them, in order.
**Per width:** `size={{ base: 'heading-3', md: 'heading-2' }}` for a heading that's smaller on phones (a listing's title bar), and `align="center"` to centre its lines.
**With Section:** give the heading an `id` and pass it to Section's `labelledBy`, so the section is a region named by its heading.
whenNotToUse: Not for emphasis or a big number in body text: use Text (or a component such as PropertyPrice).
Don't pick a level for its look: choose the level from the outline and set `size` for the look.
Don't skip levels (h1 then h3); screen-reader users lose their place.
Inside components that render their own headings (PropertyHeader, Dialog, Footer), pass `headingLevel` to them instead.

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: An icon-only button for compact, familiar actions: save a listing, go to the next photo, share, close. It always has an accessible name: `label` is required, and the code won't compile without it. Three variants cover where it sits: **plain** in toolbars and cards, **overlay** on photos, **primary** for the search submit.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, read by screen readers ("Save listing", "Next photo"). Required: the audit found 481 of 533 icon-only buttons had no accessible name.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon from the registry (src/icons). Hidden from screen readers; `label` names the button.

props.name: variant
props.description: plain: no container (toolbars, cards). overlay: translucent circle over photos. primary: dark blue fill (search submit).

props.name: size
props.description: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px square.

props.name: shape
props.description: 'circle' rounds the primary variant (plain and overlay are always circles), e.g. a submit inside a pill-shaped search field.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Can't be pressed or focused; explain why nearby.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Runs on mouse, touch and keyboard (Enter, Space) alike.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Makes it a toggle (e.g. save): announced as pressed or not pressed.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigates instead of acting, so it renders a real link.

whenToUse: **Plain:** familiar actions in toolbars, cards and headers (share, close).
**Overlay:** controls on top of photos (carousel arrows, save on a listing photo). The translucent white circle keeps the icon readable on any image.
**Primary:** the search submit inside the location field. Use `shape="circle"` inside a pill-shaped field (the hero search), where square corners would poke past the curve.
**As a toggle** (`isSelected` + `onChange`): actions that switch on and off, like save. The icon turns dark blue and fills when on, and screen readers hear "pressed".
**With `href`:** when it navigates. It renders a real link.
whenNotToUse: When the icon isn't universally understood. Use a Button with a label instead.
For the main action in a region. Use a primary Button: words beat icons for important actions.
Don't use a toggle for actions that happen once (like "share"); use a plain button.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Links take people somewhere: another page, a section, an outside site. Four variants replace the 21 link styles on AcmeCo today. Links take their size and weight from the text around them, so they add no new type styles.

props.name: children
props.description: The link text: say where it goes ("View all office listings"), never "click here".

props.name: variant
props.description: inline: inside body text, always underlined. standalone: on its own, underlined on hover. subtle: ink text for card titles and navigation, underlined on hover. inverse: white, on dark surfaces.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab, with an icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.

props.name: isCurrent
props.description: The page the reader is on (a navigation link): announced as "current page" and underlined, not shown by colour alone.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon before the text, sized to it (a view switch: "Map" with a map, "Gallery" with a grid). Decorative: the text names the link.

whenToUse: **Inline:** inside sentences ("See the **building's floor plans**"). Always underlined.
**Standalone:** on its own line or beside a heading ("View all office listings").
**Subtle:** listing titles in cards and navigation items, where the context already says "this is clickable". Ink colour, underlined on hover. Keeps AcmeCo's familiar bold black titles.
**Inverse:** on dark surfaces such as the auction banner or a dark footer.
**External:** set `external` when the link leaves AcmeCo or opens a new tab.
With `icon`, a view switch that has its own address: the search results' "Map" (map icon) and "Gallery" (grid icon). The icon is decorative; the text names the link.
whenNotToUse: For actions that change something (save, send, apply), use a Button.
For a link that should look like a button ("View documents"), use a Button with `href`.
Don't use subtle links inside body text: without the underline and colour, they're invisible there.

components.name: List
components.summary: A bullet list with AcmeCo's dark blue bullets: a listing's Highlights and its Features and Amenities. It closes the property page's list gap (decision 50).

props.name: items
props.description: The points, in reading order.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns: one number for every width, or { base, md } for phones and from 768px. Items run down the first column, then the next, as AcmeCo's two lists do.

whenToUse: For short points about one thing, in no particular order: a listing's highlights, the amenities of a building.
`columns={{ base: 1, md: 2 }}` for longer points (AcmeCo's Highlights: two columns on desktop, one on phones); more columns for single words (amenities).
whenNotToUse: Not for steps in order: those need a numbered list.
Not for label / value pairs: that's FactList.
Not for navigation links: those are a NavigationBar or the Footer.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A panel that opens from a button and sits next to it: AcmeCo's header menu now, the filter dropdowns later. White, 8px corners, the raised shadow and a 1px line, the same as the Select's list, so every panel in the system looks the same (decision 36).

props.name: trigger
props.description: The button that opens it: a Button or IconButton from the system.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the panel for screen readers ("Menu").

props.name: children
props.description: The panel's content. A function receives `close`, for content that should close it (a link that opens a dialog).

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the panel sits against the button (default: under it, right edges aligned).

whenToUse: A short set of links or controls that belongs to one button (the site menu, a filter's options).
When the page should stay in view around it.
whenNotToUse: A task with its own title and actions (a form, a confirmation): a Dialog.
Choosing one value from a list: a Select (it has its own list).
Content people need while they work on the page: put it on the page.

components.name: SearchField
components.summary: A search box: a TextField with a clear button (AcmeCo's filled dark circle with a white cross), Escape to clear and Enter to search. With `showSubmit` it adds the dark blue Search button inside its end edge, as in the hero location search.

props.name: label
props.description: Always required: the field's accessible name ("City, ZIP or address").

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hide the label visually (screen readers still get it), e.g. in the hero where the purpose is obvious.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Runs on Enter, and on the submit button when `showSubmit` is set.

props.name: showSubmit
props.description: Adds a dark blue Search button inside the field's end edge (the hero search).

props.name: submitAppearance
props.description: button: a filled dark blue circle (the hero, the default). icon: a plain dark blue magnifier (the results search, as AcmeCo's).

props.name: startIcon
props.description: An icon before the text (the results search's location arrow, from the registry). Hidden from screen readers.

props.name: size
props.description: md 40px, lg 48px.

props.name: shape
props.description: 'pill' is only for the hero location search.

whenToUse: Location and keyword searches.
The hero search: `size="lg"`, `shape="pill"`, `showSubmit`, and `hideLabel` (the purpose is obvious there).

**The results search, proposed** (decision 45): `shape="pill"`, `showSubmit` and `startIcon={<Navigation />}`: the location arrow and the hero's dark blue Search button, so searching again is as obvious on the results as on the home page.
**The results search as AcmeCo has it today** (decision 42): the same with `submitAppearance="icon"` (a plain dark blue magnifier). Use it to show AcmeCo as it is.
whenNotToUse: Filtering a short list that's already on screen: a Select or Chips may be clearer.
Free text that isn't a search (a message): use TextField.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A button that opens a list to pick one option. Two appearances: **field**, for forms, looks and behaves like TextField (it shares its tokens); **compact**, a 32px pill for sort and filter triggers, sits beside filter chips. Every dropdown on AcmeCo today is custom-built; this one gets the keyboard and screen reader behaviour custom dropdowns usually miss.

props.name: label
props.description: Always required: the visible label (field) or the trigger's text before a choice (compact), and the accessible name.

props.name: appearance
props.description: field: a form control that looks like TextField. compact: a 32px pill trigger for sort and filters.

props.name: size
props.description: Field only: md 40px, lg 48px.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Field only: shown before a choice is made.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hide the label visually (screen readers still get it). Compact triggers always do, showing it as the trigger text instead.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, the select is invalid: red, thicker border, icon and this message.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens the list on first render (used for documentation and tests).

whenToUse: One choice from about 5 to 15 options: property type, sort order, price range.
**Field** in forms (with a label above). **Compact** for sorting and filtering results, where the trigger shows its label ("Sort") until a choice is made.
whenNotToUse: Two to four options, all worth seeing at once: a TabSelector.
Several choices: a CheckboxGroup.
Very long lists that people search (cities, addresses): a search field with suggestions (later).
Navigation menus: a menu button (later), not a Select.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Rows of the same facts, compared column by column: AcmeCo's All Available Spaces. The audit found five designs for this one table on property pages and listing options (F24); this is one. It closes the property page's spaces gap (decision 47). A row can open its details: the property page opens a Dialog with the space's facts.

props.name: label
props.description: The table's name, when no heading names it.

props.name: labelledBy
props.description: The id of the heading that names the table ("All Available Spaces").

props.name: onRowAction
props.description: Pressing a row (or Enter on it) acts on it: opens the space's details. Rows get a hover state.

whenToUse: To compare several things fact by fact: the spaces in a building (Space, Size, Rental Rate, Space Use, Available).
With `onRowAction` when each row has more to show: pressing the row, or its Details button, opens it.
whenNotToUse: Not for facts about one thing: that's FactList.
Not on phones: five columns don't fit 375px. Show each row as a Card with a FactList there, as AcmeCo's phone listing does.
Not for layout. A table is for data with column headings.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between panels of related content in the same place: AcmeCo's "Language and Region" and "Currency" in the globe dialog. The current tab is in ink with AcmeCo's 2px dark blue underline; the others are grey, over a 1px line (decision 36).

props.name: label
props.description: Names the set of tabs for screen readers ("Language and currency").

props.name: items
props.description: Two to five tabs, each with its panel.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: Controlled selection (the selected tab's id).

whenToUse: Two to five panels of the same kind, where people look at one at a time (language or currency; overview, spaces, documents).
Inside a dialog or a page section; the tabs' label names the set for screen readers.
whenNotToUse: **To set a value** (For Sale / For Lease / Auctions as a search mode): that's a TabSelector, which is a radio group.
For navigation to other pages: use links (NavigationBar).
When people need to compare panels side by side: show them together.

components.name: TabSelector
components.summary: AcmeCo's grey folder tabs, used to make one choice, as in **For Sale / For Lease / Auctions** at the top of the expanded filters panel. The selected tab is white and opens into the panel below. It keeps AcmeCo's look, measured from the live site's own CSS, and replaces the other two ways the site makes the same choice (blue text links that fail contrast, and a dropdown, which Select now covers).

props.name: label
props.description: Always required: what's being chosen ("Listing type"); the group's accessible name.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label above the tabs. Usually hidden: the tab labels explain themselves.

props.name: options
props.description: Two to four short options.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Equal-width tabs across the container.

whenToUse: Choosing the search mode or listing type at the top of a panel whose content depends on it.
Two to four short options, where all of them should be visible.
`fullWidth` when the tabs should span the panel.
whenNotToUse: More than four options, or long labels: use Select.
Several choices at once: use a CheckboxGroup.
Moving between sections of a page with different content (Overview / Spaces / Location): true tabs (later), which also manage the panels.
Inside a filter bar: use a compact Select ("For Sale ⌄"), as AcmeCo already does there.

components.name: Text
components.summary: Paragraphs and inline text in the system's type styles: **body** (16/24), **body-large** (18/27), **body-small** (14/21) and **caption** (12/18), in two tones, **default** (ink) and **subtle** (the secondary grey). No margins: the layout primitives set the space between paragraphs. Bold inside it uses the loaded semibold. Found missing by the page shell pilot (gap 2, decision 38).

props.name: size
props.description: body (16/24) for most text; body-large (18/27) for an introduction; body-small (14/21) for secondary detail; caption (12/18) for fine print. One size, or one per width ({ base: 'body-small', md: 'body-large' }).

props.name: align
props.description: start (the default) or center.

props.name: tone
props.description: default: ink. subtle: the secondary grey, for supporting detail (still 4.5:1 or more).

props.name: as
props.description: p for a paragraph (the default), span for text inside a line, div for a block that holds other elements.

whenToUse: **body** for most text on a page.
**body-large** for a short introduction under a page title.
**body-small** for secondary detail (a note under a form, a listing's description in a list).
**caption** for fine print (disclaimers, photo credits).
**subtle** for supporting text that shouldn't compete with the main text.
**Per width:** `size={{ base: 'body-small', md: 'body-large' }}`, and `align="center"` for a centred line (a title bar).
**as="span"** inside a line, **as="div"** for a block that holds other elements.
whenNotToUse: Not for headings: use Heading, so the page has an outline.
Not for labels of controls: fields, buttons and links bring their own text.
Don't use subtle for anything people must read to act (prices, errors, instructions).
Don't space paragraphs with margins or empty lines; put them in a Stack.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: A labelled field for typing: a name, an email address, a message to a broker. One shape (outlined, 4px corners) replaces the five AcmeCo uses today. It shares its label, hint, error and border with every other form control, so they all look and behave alike.

props.name: label
props.description: Always required: the visible label, and the field's accessible name.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hide the label visually (screen readers still get it). Only when the purpose is obvious from context, such as the hero location search.

props.name: hint
props.description: Short help below the field ("We'll only use this to reply to you").

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, the field is invalid: red, thicker border, icon and this message. Say how to fix it.

props.name: multiline

Put it in a `DialogTrigger` with the control that opens it, or control it with `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`.

`onContinue(email)` receives a valid address; the next step (password or new account) is the caller's. `onProvider(name)` receives the chosen option; `providers` lists the options with their placeholder marks.
whenNotToUse: Not before someone has asked for something that needs an account: don't open it on page load.
Not for contacting a broker: guests can send the contact form without an account (the benchmark lesson 10).
